questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question:
A particle having electric charge \(3\times 10^{-19}~\text{C}\) and mass \(6\times 10^{-27}~\text{kg}\) is accelerated by applying an electric potential of \(1.21~\text{V}\). Wavelength of the matter wave associated with the particle is \(\alpha\times 10^{-12}~\text{m}.\) The value of \(\alpha\) is:
(Take Planck’s constant \(= 6.6\times 10^{-34}~\text{J.s}\))
1. \(10\)
2. \(15\)
3. \(20\)
4. \(25\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(\lambda=\dfrac{{h}}{\sqrt{2 mqV}}\) Step:Find the value of\(\alpha\). For a particle accelerated through potential\(V\), the kinetic energy of the particle is given by; \(\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = qV\) \(\Rightarrow p =mv = \sqrt{2mqV}\) The de-Broglie wavelength of the particle is given by; \(\lambda=\dfrac{{h}}{\sqrt{2 mqV}}\) \(\Rightarrow \lambda=\dfrac{6.6 \times 10^{-34}}{\sqrt{2 \times 18 \times 10^{-46} \times 1.21}}\) \(\Rightarrow \lambda=10^{-11}~\text{m} = 10\times 10^{-12}~\text{m}\) Therefore, the value of\(\alpha \)is\(10.\) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Two electrons are moving with non-relativistic speeds in mutually perpendicular directions. If their respective de-Broglie wavelengths are \(\lambda_1\)​ and \(\lambda_2,\) then their de-Broglie wavelength in the centre-of-mass frame is:
1.\(\dfrac{1}{\lambda_{\mathrm{com}}}=\dfrac{1}{\lambda_1}+\dfrac{1}{\lambda_2}\)2.\(\lambda_{\mathrm{com}}=\dfrac { 2 \lambda_1 \lambda_2 }{ \sqrt {\lambda^2_1 + \lambda^2_2}}\)
3.\(\lambda_{\mathrm{com}}= \lambda_1= \lambda_2\)4.\(\lambda_{\mathrm{com}} = \bigg(\dfrac{\lambda_1 +\lambda_2}{2}\bigg)\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(\lambda_\text{com}=\dfrac{h}{mv_\text{com}}\) Step: Find the de-Broglie wavelength in the frame of reference attached to their centre of mass. For the two electrons, the momentum of the particle is given by; \(p_1 = \dfrac{h}{\lambda_1}, p_2 = \dfrac{h}{\lambda_2}\) The electrons move perpendicular, so momenta are perpendicular. The relative momentum of the electron is given by; \(p_\text{rel}= |\vec p_1 -\vec p_2|\) \(\Rightarrow p_\text{rel}= \sqrt{p^2_1+ p^2_2}~~~~~~[\text{As electrons are moving perpendicular}]\) For two identical particles, the momentum of each in COM frame equals half the relative momentum. \(p_\text{com}= \dfrac{1}{2}p_\text{rel}\) \(\Rightarrow p_\text{com}= \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{p^2_1+ p^2_2}\) \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{h}{\lambda_\text{com}}= \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{h}{\lambda_1}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{h}{\lambda_2}\right)^2}\) \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\lambda_\text{com}}= \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{\lambda^2_1+\lambda^2_2 }{\lambda^2_1\lambda^2_1}}\) \(\Rightarrow{\lambda_\text{com}}={\dfrac{{2}{\lambda_1\lambda_1}}{\sqrt{\lambda^2_1+\lambda^2_2 }}}\) Hence, option (2) is the correct answer.

questions.question:

3.\(1:1\)4.\(2:3\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(\lambda=\frac{h}{p} \) Explanation:Since the nucleus is initially at rest, its initial linear momentum is zero. Furthermore, since the de-Broglie wavelength is inversely proportional to momentum i.e., \(\lambda \propto \frac{1}{p}\). Therefore, the de-Broglie wavelength of the two parts will be the same. Hence, option (3) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
An electron and proton are separated by a large distance. The electron starts approaching the proton with energy \(3~\text{eV}.\) The proton captures the electron and forms a hydrogen atom in the second excited state. The resulting photon is incident on a photosensitive metal of threshold wavelength \(4000 \mathring{A}.\)  Then the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectron is:
1. \(1.41~\text{eV}\)
2. \(7.61~\text{eV}\)
3. \(3.3~\text{eV}\)
4. no photoelectron would be emitted
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(K.E_\text{max}=h\nu-\phi \) Step 1:Find the energy of electron in second excited state of hydrogen atom. \(E_3=-\dfrac{13.6}{3^2}\text{ eV}\) \(\Rightarrow E_3=-1.51\text{ eV}\) Step 2:Find the energy of resulting photon. Conservation of energy: \(3=-1.51+E\) \(\Rightarrow E=4.51\text{ eV}\) Step 3:Find the work function of photosensitive metal. \(\phi=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}\) \(\Rightarrow \phi=\dfrac{12400}{4000}\) \(\Rightarrow \phi=\dfrac{12.4}{4}=3.1\text{ eV}\) Step 4:Find the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectron. \(E=K+\phi\) \(\Rightarrow 4.51=K+3.1\) \(\Rightarrow K=1.41\text{ eV}\) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.
